skill.name: css-development-refactor
skill.description: Refactors existing CSS from inline styles or utility class repetition into semantic component classes with dark mode support and tests.
skill.summary: Refactor CSS into semantic component patterns with dark mode and behavior checks.

**Action:** Read `styles/components.css` to see if patterns already exist
**Action:** Create new semantic classes in `styles/components.css` for patterns that need extraction
**Action:** Ensure all new/refactored classes have `dark:` variants

content.value_statement: Repeated utility classes and inline styles make frontend code harder to maintain. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through semantic CSS refactoring with tests.
actual_capabilities: Identifies inline styles and repeated utility class combinations in component markup.
Converts repeated patterns into semantic CSS classes using Tailwind composition.
Checks existing component styles before creating new CSS classes.
Adds dark mode variants for refactored component styles.
Updates markup to use semantic class names while preserving custom classes.
Recommends static CSS tests and component rendering tests for refactored styles.
limitations: It depends on the agent reading project files and understanding the existing CSS structure.
It does not guarantee pixel-perfect visual parity without screenshots or manual review.
It assumes Tailwind or compatible utility composition is available when using @apply.
It provides workflow guidance and examples, not a standalone automated refactoring engine.

use_cases.title: Clean Up Utility-Heavy Components
use_cases.description: Convert repeated utility class strings into reusable semantic classes for easier maintenance.

use_cases.title: Add Dark Mode During Refactoring
use_cases.description: Extend refactored classes with dark mode variants while preserving the existing light theme.

use_cases.title: Prepare Safer Style Migrations
use_cases.description: Document changed selectors, add tests, and verify behavior before merging CSS cleanup work.

prompt_templates.title: Find CSS Refactor Targets
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to inspect my components and list repeated inline styles or utility class groups that should become semantic CSS classes.

prompt_templates.title: Extract Semantic Classes
prompt_templates.scenario: Convert repeated utilities into component classes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor the repeated button and card utility classes into semantic CSS classes. Reuse existing components.css patterns before creating new classes.

prompt_templates.title: Add Dark Mode Coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the new semantic CSS classes and add dark mode variants for backgrounds, borders, text, hover, and focus states where needed.

prompt_templates.title: Complete Verified Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor the selected CSS patterns, update markup, add static CSS and rendering tests, then summarize changed files and behavior verification results.

output_examples.input: A component repeats the same long button utility classes in many files.
output_examples.output: The skill identifies the repeated pattern, proposes a semantic button class, updates markup, and recommends tests for the new selector.

output_examples.input: A card layout has light theme styles but no dark mode support.
output_examples.output: The skill adds matching dark mode variants, documents the semantic class purpose, and asks for visual verification in both themes.

output_examples.input: A team needs a summary after a CSS cleanup branch.
output_examples.output: The skill reports created classes, updated files, test coverage, behavior checks, and practical next steps for review.

best_practices: Start with repeated patterns and preserve one-off utility classes unless extraction improves maintainability.
Check existing component styles before adding new classes or variants.
Verify refactored styles with tests and visual review in light and dark modes.
anti_patterns: Do not rename classes without updating every affected component and test.
Do not create semantic classes that only wrap a single unrelated one-off style.
Do not claim behavior is unchanged without running available tests or reviewing the UI.

faq.question: Does this skill require Tailwind CSS?
faq.answer: It is written for Tailwind-style @apply composition, but the workflow can guide other semantic CSS refactors.

faq.question: Can it remove all utility classes?
faq.answer: No. It recommends keeping one-off utilities when a semantic class would add unnecessary abstraction.

faq.question: Does it edit project files automatically?
faq.answer: It instructs the agent to read files, apply focused edits, add tests, and verify behavior when tools are available.

faq.question: How does it handle dark mode?
faq.answer: It asks the agent to add dark variants for backgrounds, text, borders, and interactive states in new classes.

faq.question: What tests does it suggest?
faq.answer: It suggests static CSS tests for selectors and rendering tests that confirm components use the new semantic classes.

faq.question: Is it safe for large refactors?
faq.answer: It can guide large refactors, but changes should be split, tested, and visually reviewed before merging.
